methodology: MVP: Sleeper player search rank + actual league production (when available) + roster fit + starting-lineup impact.
headline: Kamara Package Edges Rice in a Classic Need-for-Need Swap
verdict: Parker is the current winner, though the gap is narrow rather than decisive.
summary: Parker gets the stronger overall grade, 83.3 to Joey’s 73.2, and the larger package-value return: 101.9 for a single player valued at 55.2. Kamara brings the best supplied production in the deal, averaging 9.4 points for the season and 10.2 recently, while Dowdle adds another running back after Parker sent away a wide receiver. That fit matters for a 2-5 team carrying seven RBs but only four WRs, even if the lineup-impact score is a modest 70. Joey’s 3-4 roster has seven wideouts and five backs, so Rice addresses a positional imbalance, but his recent average is listed at zero. The league’s Public Enemy may have survived another trade headline.

Parker’s roster has seven running backs but only four wide receivers, so the fit is not perfect; still, the 2-5 team receives the deal’s strongest actual production indicators and more total value. The 70 lineup-impact score keeps this from being a runaway, but King of Dogshit Trades gets to enjoy a rare favorable headline.
